Hi Olivia — thanks for the sample and clear problem statement. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- Use case: semantic search over product docs (short queries, paraphrase-heavy).
- Key success metrics: top-5 precision/recall on annotated query set, MRR, and embedding cosine margin between paraphrase vs. unrelated pairs.

Model recommendations (start with these 3):
1) open-embed-small-v2 (128d / quantized) — cost-efficient, good for latency-sensitive workloads.
2) open-embed-medium-v1 (384d) — better semantic capacity for paraphrase detection.
3) open-embed-large-pt (1024d / fp16) — best quality baseline to measure headroom.

Evaluation plan (1-week pilot):
- Day 0–1: ingest sample, run baseline eval with your current embeddings (we'll run locally on the sample).
- Day 2–4: generate embeddings for the 3 candidate models, run semantic search benchmarks (top-k precision@5, MRR), and nearest-neighbor drift checks.
- Day 5: present results + recommended operating point (model + dimensionality + quantization tradeoffs) and draft cost/latency estimates for production.

Attachments / links:
- Prompt set & eval checklist (prompt-set-v2.txt) — includes recommended annotation queries and paraphrase pairs.
- Benchmark dashboard (drive link): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcdBenchmark

Notes on dimensionality & drift:
- Lower-d models can be surprisingly robust if your corpus is high-signal and queries are short — but they lose capacity for fine-grained paraphrase distinctions.
- We'll add a small drift probe (simulate content change) to measure embedding stability across releases.

Next steps:
1) If this plan looks good, can you confirm access to a 50k query set (or confirm we can upsample from the sample)?
2) Agree to the pilot dates (we can start as early as Tue 2026-01-20).

I'll loop Marissa for the detailed metric definitions and Rishi for cost/infra sizing.

Thanks,

Hi team — adding a few concrete metric definitions and a quick note on drift checks.

Metrics (we'll compute these for each model):
- Precision@5 (annotated queries) — primary metric for search relevance.
- MRR (mean reciprocal rank) — helpful for ranking impact.
- Cosine margin (paraphrase vs. random) — captures representational gap.
- Recall@100 for broad retrieval tasks.

Drift / dimensionality considerations:
- We'll run a PCA on the embeddings to inspect explained variance vs. dimensionality. If you see >90% explained variance in the top 100 components for a 1024d model, you might safely reduce dims with minimal loss.
- We'll also run a rolling drift probe: resample queries across your release snapshots (last 6 months) and compute centroid shifts and average nearest-neighbor distance changes. Significant shifts (>15% change in avg NN distance) are a red flag for retrain cadence.

I've attached an export of recent internal benchmark runs (embeddings-benchmarks.csv) showing a similar customer where medium (384d) hit a good latency/quality sweet spot.

If Searchly confirms the 50k dataset, we can provision the pilot infra estimate — Rishi, can you add a quick cost/latency table for the three models?

Thanks,
Marissa
